scope: Offline source-only audit of js/spb-ai-lease.js and bounded actual functions from js/spb-pro-ai.js. No production, mirror, Wiki, native UI, or provider changes were made.

source_freeze.note: The pro-AI file hash changed after first observation and before test hash pinning, despite this review making no edits to it. The contract pins the later 115F… hash; findings should be rechecked against the source state intended for integration.

test.result: FAIL 7/10 scenarios passed; three lifecycle invariants failed.
test.harness: Runs extracted actual runTurn/runTurn2/ask/finish/finishCore/mcpCall/previewOptions and the actual cancel-handler branch, plus the actual lease module in VM. Provider responses are fake controllable Promises. Tool-callback queue collection, renderer/UI effects, and applyQueue are test doubles; applyQueue records current doc id and queue. No actual provider, canvas mutation, or native browser was used.

findings.evidence: Actual Cancel branch at js/spb-pro-ai.js:2721 sets _cancelOpts=true and aborts _ctl. The ordinary runTurn2 path calls AI.run at js/spb-pro-ai.js:691 and handles successful completion without checking _cancelOpts at js/spb-pro-ai.js:692. Actual finishCore applies the returned queue at js/spb-pro-ai.js:748 without a cancellation-generation guard.
findings.probe: Fake provider intentionally ignores AbortSignal, resolves successfully after Cancel; the real extracted ask/runTurn2/finish path applies its queue (1 recorded write; expected 0).
findings.impact: If a provider does not promptly honor AbortSignal, a user-canceled request may still paint. Cancel currently behaves as best-effort transport abort rather than revoking request authority.

findings.evidence: AI.run(opts) is invoked at js/spb-pro-ai.js:691 before the Promise success/rejection handlers are attached at :692.
findings.probe: Fake AI.run throws synchronously. ask rejects, `_busy` remains true and `_ctl` remains set; expected busy false and controller cleared.
findings.impact: A synchronous adapter/configuration failure can leave the composer locked in its working state.

findings.evidence: finishCore only applies document/element identity validation when `entryOpts.elementRunIdentity` exists (guard at js/spb-pro-ai.js:711 and element guard at :747). Ordinary requests reach unconditional applyQueue at :748.
findings.probe: Start an ordinary ask on doc-A, change the harness current document to doc-B before resolving the fake provider, then invoke actual finish. applyQueue receives a write while current doc id is doc-B (expected 0 writes). The same test with an elementRunIdentity correctly rejects the changed target.
findings.impact: A slow ordinary answer can be applied to whichever document is active at completion, rather than the document that supplied its context.

passing_checks: Normal delayed provider completion invokes the apply path once and clears busy.
Abort-aware provider rejects on Stop; old request does not write and a subsequent request starts.
Asynchronous provider rejection returns an error and clears busy/controller.
Element-scoped delayed response rejects changed element identity before apply.
External lease stays exclusive through active work even after the nominal 120-second idle TTL; settlement releases busy and permits later takeover.
External MCP core rejection returns a failure and releases busy/lease even when render is missing.
Cancel during delayed option preview restores the snapshot, skips later previews, and clears busy.
limitations: This is a bounded VM harness, not a full Electron/DOM or live app test. It cannot prove renderer usability or actual canvas mutation behavior.
The tool queue is injected after the fake provider response because no actual model tool callback is exercised; actual finishCore and its apply decision are exercised.
The document-switch finding proves the extracted helper invokes applyQueue in the new-document state; a real applyQueue implementation may have independent guards not included in this W10 boundary.
The lease helper has no timeout for an active call. The review confirmed active lease exclusivity but did not simulate browser process termination or abandoned active state recovery.
